paraphrases.title: MG996R servo mount with gussets
paraphrases.request: Heavy-duty MG996R servo mount (body 40.7 x 19.7 x 42.9 mm, tabs 53.6 mm long, tab holes 49.5 mm apart, output shaft up) to sit on top of 2020 aluminium extrusion, 300 mm or longer. The servo lowers straight into a pocket in a printed block, 0.3 mm clearance per side, tabs on the block top. Four M4 socket-head bolts hold it through the tab holes: two per tab, 49.5 mm apart along the tab, 10 mm apart across. The block stands on a flange bolted into the extrusion T-slot with two M5 bolts and T-nuts. Two gussets support the block against a 1.5 N m servo torque reaction. Show the load path from servo to extrusion bolts. PLA, FDM, no supports.
paraphrases.request_notes: Added to the plan brief, all from requirements.md section 3: servo output axis vertical with the tabs on the block top (FD1); four tab holes, two per tab (A2); M5 bolts and T-nuts into the top slot (FD2, A4); PLA and FDM (A9). Audit: the cross-tab hole spacing (A2) is now in the request and in part.json.

l1.text: Place the catalogue servo, extrusion, two T-nuts and the bolts, output shaft vertical, and declare the layout.
Servo drops straight down into a block pocket. Clearance 0.3 mm per side around the body; 0.3 to 2.5 mm between servo and pocket floor; tabs sit on top of the block.
Four M4 bolts through the four tab holes into block pilot holes fix the servo. Each bolt reachable by screwdriver.
No printed material in the servo's cable exit, output spline or horn sweep.

Block sits on a flange lying flat on the extrusion, held by two M5 bolts through clearance holes into T-nuts in the top slot, on its centreline. Bolts 60 to 110 mm apart along the slot, output spline between them in X. Each bolt long enough to engage its nut but short of the slot floor. Flange at least 3 mm around each bolt head.

Two gussets link block and flange, one per side of the block. Thickness 3 to 8 mm, length along the flange 10 mm or more, height up the block 15 mm or more. Together they give the block-to-flange section at least 1.25 times the bending stiffness (second moment of area about the axis along the extrusion) of the block footprint by itself.

Must withstand 1.5 N m servo torque reaction. State the load path: servo, M4 bolts, block, gussets, flange, two M5 extrusion bolts, within stress, bearing and bolt limits. Limits and model: PLA thread shear 4 MPa on the pilot cylinder (tab-bolt thread strength at least 3 times bolt shear; bolts share torque in proportion to distance from the centroid of the four holes); block-to-flange junction 2 MPa shear and 3 MPa bending; bearing under an M5 head 5 MPa; 500 N tension per T-nut. Horn side force is torque divided by the 25 mm horn reach, acting across the extrusion at horn plate mid-height and tipping the mount about the extrusion edge (10 mm from the bolt line); the two M5 bolts carry it in proportion to their X distance from the spline.
Loosen the M5 bolts and the T-nuts and mount slide along the slot. Every M5 bolt reachable by screwdriver.
One manifold body, FDM printable without supports.
Size limit 130 x 70 x 45 mm.
Deliver an STL (assembly pose), OpenSCAD source, declared layout, load-path statement and the agent's own clearance report. Report and statement must match an independent measurement.

beyond_library: catalogue placement of a servo, an extrusion with a T-slot cavity, T-nuts and bolts by datums
subtraction: a pocket, a cable channel, blind pilots and through holes
tolerance stack: bolt length against flange thickness, lip thickness, nut thickness and slot depth
load path: statics from the measured mesh with stated allowable stresses
interference checks against keep-out volumes (horn sweep, cable exit), driver columns and a drop-in sweep

paraphrases.title: MG996R servo mount with gussets
paraphrases.request: Please design a sturdy mount for an MG996R servo, which sits on the top of a piece of 2020 aluminium extrusion that is at least 300 mm long. The servo itself is 40.7 x 19.7 x 42.9 mm, its mounting ears span 53.6 mm with the holes 49.5 mm apart, and the output shaft points upward. It goes straight down into a pocket in a printed block with 0.3 mm to spare on each side, and the ears sit on the upper surface of the block. Four M4 socket-head bolts secure it through the ear holes, two in each ear, 49.5 mm apart along the ear and 10 mm apart across it. The block is mounted on a flange, and that flange is fastened in the extrusion's T-slot with two M5 bolts and T-nuts. Add two gussets so the block can take a servo torque reaction of 1.5 N m, and lay out the load path running from the servo down to the extrusion bolts. Print in PLA on an FDM machine without supports.
paraphrases.request_notes: Added to the plan brief, all from requirements.md section 3: servo output axis vertical with the tabs on the block top (FD1); four tab holes, two per tab (A2); M5 bolts and T-nuts into the top slot (FD2, A4); PLA and FDM (A9). Audit: the cross-tab hole spacing (A2) is now in the request and in part.json.

l1.text: From the parts catalogue, place the servo, the extrusion, a pair of T-nuts and the bolts, with the servo's output shaft upright, and declare that layout.

The servo must go straight down into a pocket in the block, with 0.3 mm of clearance around the body on every side and 0.3 to 2.5 mm of space under its bottom, and its ears must rest on top of the block.
Four M4 bolts through the servo's four ear holes into pilot holes in the block hold it in place, and a screwdriver must be able to reach each one.
Keep the servo's cable exit, output spline and horn sweep clear of any printed material.

The block rests on a flange sitting flat on the extrusion, secured by two M5 bolts passing through clearance holes into T-nuts in the extrusion's top slot, along its centreline. The bolts sit 60 to 110 mm apart along the slot, with the servo's output spline between them in X. Each bolt must be long enough to engage its nut yet not reach the slot floor, and the flange must extend 3 mm or more around each bolt head.

Put one gusset on each side of the block, tying it to the flange. Each is 3 to 8 mm thick, at least 10 mm long along the flange and at least 15 mm high up the block. With both, the block-to-flange section must be at least 1.25 times as stiff in bending (second moment of area about the axis along the extrusion) as the block footprint alone.

The mount has to survive a 1.5 N m servo torque reaction. Spell out the load path from the servo through the M4 bolts, the block, the gussets and the flange to the two M5 extrusion bolts, and keep it inside the stress, bearing and bolt limits. Use this model and these limits. Thread shear in PLA is 4 MPa on the pilot cylinder; the tab-bolt thread strength must be at least 3 times the bolt shear, with the bolts sharing the torque according to how far each is from the centroid of the four holes. In the block-to-flange junction allow 2 MPa shear and 3 MPa bending. Under an M5 head allow 5 MPa bearing, and 500 N tension for each T-nut. The side force at the horn is the torque divided by a 25 mm horn reach; it acts across the extrusion at the mid-height of the horn plate and tips the mount about the extrusion's edge, which is 10 mm from the bolt line. The two M5 bolts carry it in proportion to their X distance from the spline.
With the M5 bolts slackened, the T-nuts and the mount should slide along the slot, and a screwdriver should reach every M5 bolt.
The mount must be a single manifold body that can be printed on an FDM printer with no supports.
The mount must not exceed 130 x 70 x 45 mm.

Deliverables are an STL in the assembly pose, the OpenSCAD source, the declared layout, the load-path statement and the agent's own clearance report. The report and the statement must both agree with an independent measurement.
